title: k-Nearest Neighbors
interviewAnswer: k-NN predicts using nearby training examples. It is simple and non-parametric but sensitive to feature scaling, irrelevant dimensions and inference cost on large datasets.
why: k-NN is a simple non-parametric method that exposes distance metrics, scaling, curse of dimensionality and latency trade-offs.
intuition: To predict a new point, find the nearest training examples and let their labels/values vote. The model stores data rather than learning many parameters.
deepDive: Small k gives flexible high-variance boundaries; large k smooths predictions and increases bias. Feature scaling is critical because distance is coordinate-dependent. In high dimensions, distances concentrate and nearest-neighbor meaning degrades. Exact search is expensive for large datasets, motivating trees or approximate nearest-neighbor indexes.
workedExample: If one feature ranges 0–1 and another 0–100000, Euclidean distance is dominated by the large-scale feature unless you normalize appropriately.
code:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
m=make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=7))
commonMistakes: Using raw unscaled features with heterogeneous units.
Assuming k-NN training is expensive—it is inference/storage that often dominates.
production: k-NN can be latency/memory heavy at scale; vector indexes and embedding retrieval are modern relatives with similar distance/index concerns.
